subject.title: feat(images): bake TruffleHog into Linux tooling

question: Should autoreview require a locally installed TruffleHog binary for all existing environments, or should the new scanner remain opt-in until cross-platform provisioning is established?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes an existing review entry point from self-contained behavior to a fail-closed external-tool prerequisite, and baking that tool only into Linux images does not settle the intended cross-platform support contract.

options.title: Preserve the current default
options.body: Keep autoreview usable without TruffleHog and expose scanning through an explicit opt-in until all supported environments have a maintained installation path.

options.title: Adopt a global prerequisite
options.body: Approve TruffleHog as a documented requirement for every autoreview environment and add supported installation, upgrade, and proof coverage for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

options.title: Limit the change to image provisioning
options.body: Bake and smoke-test TruffleHog in Linux images now, but defer the autoreview preflight behavior to a separately approved compatibility proposal.

recommendation.title: Preserve the current default
recommendation.body: Keep autoreview usable without TruffleHog and expose scanning through an explicit opt-in until all supported environments have a maintained installation path.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the proposed installer and autoreview synchronization and can clarify the intended rollout boundary; current-main ownership could not be established from the supplied evidence.
